title: Звонок Елены и паника поваров  (Elena's Call and the Cooks' Panic)

segments.t: Elena Pavlovna calls Viktor Petrovich to thank him for the wonderful surprise dish and agrees to meet him in an hour. Meanwhile, the cooks realize that Chef Barinov tasted the fugu fish himself and begins feeling numb, sparking full-blown panic in the kitchen.
Тогда что же, встретимся через час?
А что, там холодно, быстрее отойдет?
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
'Elena Pavlovna, forgive me, my...' Barinov proceeds sharply without holding back, so Elena knows he is not just making small talk.
'Believe me, it was absolutely delightful.' Vika stresses this clear expression right here: "voskhititelnym" means "delightful" (from "voskhititelnyy"), giving the line its exact edge.
'I am glad that you liked it.' Elena phrases this statement to Barinov: the "-sya" ending on "ponravilos" ("pleased, was liked") turns the action inward or makes it happen between people naturally.
'I thank you.' Barinov steps in boldly around Vika, watching Vika's face to see how the news lands.
'It is nothing, nothing at all, do not worry.' Vika underscores one direct element in earnest: "perezhivayte" means "worry" (from "perezhivat"), giving the line its exact edge.
'Excuse me. It is nothing.' Elena gives the thought around Vika: using the polite form "izvinite" ("excuse me, forgive me") keeps a respectful distance as Elena steps in.
'Everything is fine.' Barinov reacts warmly to settle things, bringing things back to earth after the buildup.
'Hello, Viktor Petrovich.' Vika makes this update facing Elena: spoken Russian trims this down to just 3 words, dropping the extra helper words that English has to spell out.
Тогда что же, встретимся через час?
'Then what do you say we meet in an hour?' Elena sends the thought frankly here: the "-sya" ending on "vstretimsya" ("we'll meet") turns the action inward or makes it happen between people naturally.
'I will be driving my car.' Barinov proceeds quietly across the room, saying out loud what both of them already know.
'We have to stop him.' Vika uses one pointed touch on cue: "ostanovit" means "to stop", and it carries the main weight of what Vika is saying.
'It makes no difference now.' Elena makes this warning beside Vika: spoken Russian trims this down to just 3 words, dropping the extra helper words that English has to spell out.
А что, там холодно, быстрее отойдет?
'What, since it is cold in there, will it wear off faster?' Barinov quizzes wryly about what Elena just brought up.
Тогда что же, встретимся через час?
А что, там холодно, быстрее отойдет?

That wraps up this scene as elena calls Viktor Petrovich to thank him for the delicious dish and arrange a meeting in an hour, while the cooks panic after realizing the Chef tasted the fugu himself. Until next time!
